cycles.name: Foundation Forge
focuses: Build fundamental movement patterns and establish the training habit.
Prime the nervous system and begin shifting body composition from baseline.

paragraphs: This phase is not the most exciting one. It is the most important one. Everything that happens in Cycles 2 through 5 — every strength gain, every body composition shift, every visible change — is built on what you do right now.

Foundation Forge exists to teach your body how to move correctly under load, to build the connective tissue and motor patterns that allow you to train hard later without breaking down. You are not just exercising. You are programming your nervous system.
Your job this cycle is simple: show up, move well, and do not rush. The weights will feel light. That is correct.
outcomes: Noticeably improved energy across training days
Movement patterns feel more controlled and deliberate
Sleep quality begins to shift as the body adapts to regular training
Body awareness and proprioception improve — you will feel muscles working that you couldn't before
Priority lifts tracked and baseline loads established for Cycle 2

cycles.name: Structural Build
focuses: Develop progressive strength across all major movement patterns.
Increase mechanical tension to drive visible muscle development.

paragraphs: Four months in and your body is ready for more than Cycle 1 was giving you. That block was built to teach you how to move and to see how you recover. It did its job.

The problem is the weights stopped moving in June. That's on the program, not on you. It told you to stay at an easy effort and you did exactly that, every session, honestly. Now the effort goes up on every lift.
Three days instead of four, because three is what you actually do, and I'd rather you finish every session you start. Your job this block is to get comfortable with a set that's genuinely hard.
outcomes: Hip thrust finally loaded for what your glutes can really do
A weight that goes up, not one that sits still for two months
Left arm pressing what the right one can
Comfortable working two reps from failure
Your treadmill walks written into the plan, not squeezed on the end
A video of your first hip thrust and split squat sent to me

cycles.name: Metabolic Shift
focuses: Layer metabolic demand onto the strength base to accelerate fat loss.
Improve work capacity and cardiovascular resilience.

teaser.subtitle: Once you're strong enough for it to be worth doing, we turn the pace up.
paragraphs: Cycle 3 takes the strength you build here and makes you use it faster and for longer, with less rest in between. That's where the shape change really starts to show.
But it only works on top of real strength. That's what this block is for.
Build the engine first. Then we run it.

cycles.name: Recomposition Peak
focuses: Maximise hypertrophy through increased volume and intensity.
Sharpen body composition and develop visible muscle definition.

cycles.name: Shape & Sustain
focuses: Peak the physique and consolidate all strength gains.
Build the lifestyle infrastructure to sustain results independently.

days.completionMessage: That's the hardest your glutes have worked since you started. Get some protein in and let them recover properly.

good: Keep the pace easy enough that you could hold a conversation
Just get warm and let the hips loosen up
bad: Don't race it, this isn't the workout

good: Push the floor away through the heel of the working leg
Squeeze that one glute hard at the top
bad: Don't let your hips tip to one side

good: Keep the dowel touching your head, upper back and tailbone the whole time
Feel the hamstrings take the load as the hips go back
bad: Don't lose contact at the lower back, that's the rep failing

good: Step wide and sit back into that hip, other leg stays straight
Sit into it and control how far you go, this should feel like it's opening not pulling
bad: Never push into a sharp stretch here, and don't let the stepping knee roll in

exercises.name: Barbell Hip Thrust
exercises.note: You've been at 12.5 kg since June, which is lighter than the empty bar, and your legs are a lot stronger than that. First session, start with the empty bar for 10, then add 5 kg each set. Stop at the first set that feels like a hard 8, or at 40 kg, whichever comes first. Use a bar pad, it will hurt otherwise.

good: Bench across your shoulder blades, bar padded and sitting in the crease of your hips, then drive the floor away through your heels
Squeeze the glutes hard at the top and hold for a second before you come down
bad: If your lower back is finishing the rep instead of your glutes the weight is too heavy, take some off

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.note: This has sat at 20 kg for two months at an easy effort, so it's ready to move. Go up in small steps and let the range decide, not the weight. When your back wants to round to go lower, that's the bottom.

good: Push your hips back toward the wall behind you, dumbbells brushing your legs
Feel the stretch build in the back of your thighs, stop when it runs out
bad: Don't round your back to reach lower, the range ends where your hamstrings end

good: Walk out so the cable stays tight, then drive the hips forward to standing
Finish every rep with a hard glute squeeze, not a lean back
bad: Don't turn it into a squat, knees stay soft and the hips do the moving

good: Bring your heels all the way to your glutes, then lower under control
Keep the tension in the back of your thigh the whole way down
bad: Don't let your hips lift off the pad to help the weight up

good: Straighten the legs fully and hold at the top for a second
All the burn should sit in the front of the thigh
bad: Don't swing the weight up or bang into lockout

good: Press the handle straight out from your chest and hold it still for a second
Brace your stomach so the cable can't twist you
bad: Don't let your shoulders turn toward the machine

days.completionMessage: Every press and pull today made your left arm carry its own share. That's how the gap closes.

good: Long smooth strokes, legs then back then arms
Let the shoulders and upper back warm through
bad: Don't yank with the arms first

good: Pull the band apart until it touches your chest
Squeeze between the shoulder blades
bad: Don't shrug up toward your ears

good: Move one segment of the spine at a time
Feel the mid-back open as you round
bad: Don't rush, this is slow on purpose

good: Take the band from in front of your thighs to behind your hips, arms straight
Feel the front of the shoulders open
bad: If it feels tight move your hands wider on the band, don't force it through

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.note: Pick the weight your left arm can finish all the reps with, not the one your right arm wants. The right one waits for the left to catch up. Sit the dumbbells on your thighs and kick them up one at a time to get into position.

good: Sit the dumbbells on your thighs and kick them up one at a time, then press up and slightly together over your upper chest
Feel your chest stretch at the bottom, then squeeze it to push
bad: Don't let your elbows flare straight out to the sides, keep them about 45 degrees

good: Pull the bar to your collarbone and drive your elbows down toward your back pockets
Feel your back doing the pulling, your hands are just hooks
bad: Don't lean back and rock, the torso stays almost still

exercises.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row
exercises.note: Always start with your left arm. Whatever number it does honestly is the number the right arm does too. Don't let the right one run ahead, that's how the gap stays open.

good: Row the dumbbell to your hip, not your chest, shoulders square to the floor
Feel it in the side of your back, under the armpit
bad: Don't twist your body to finish the rep

good: Press straight up so the dumbbells finish over your ears, back flat on the bench
Keep the shoulders working, don't let it turn into a tricep push
bad: Don't arch your back off the bench to get the weight up

good: Lead with your elbow and stop when your arm reaches shoulder height
The side of the shoulder should be burning, not the neck
bad: Don't shrug or swing, if you have to throw it then it's too heavy

exercises.name: Incline Treadmill Walk
exercises.note: Start at incline 4 and 5.5, same as you've been doing on your own. You should be able to talk but not sing. If you could sing, put the incline up. The notes tab has the plan for how this grows.

good: Set the incline first, then the speed, then walk tall with your eyes up
Your calves and the back of your legs should be doing the pushing on the hill
bad: Don't lean on the handrails, that takes the work out of it

days.completionMessage: Full round complete. That's the whole week's work banked, so take a proper rest day before you start again.

good: Easy pace, just get the blood moving
Let the legs wake up before you load them
bad: Don't start hard

good: Sit back like there's a chair just behind you
Weight spread evenly through the whole foot
bad: Don't let your heels lift

good: Hold your toes, drop your hips into a deep squat, then straighten the legs
Feel the hips and the back of the legs open up as you stand
bad: Don't force the depth, go as low as you can with a flat back

good: Walk your hands out to a plank, then walk your feet up to your hands
Feel the back of the legs lengthen on the way in
bad: Don't let the hips sag in the plank position

exercises.name: Machine Leg Press
exercises.note: First session, use a light weight and find the depth where your lower back stays flat on the pad. That's your bottom from now on and it doesn't get deeper as the weight goes up. Cap the first session around 160 lb and add no more than 10 lb per session after that. Set the safety catches before your first set.

good: Push through your whole foot and stop just short of locking the knees
Feel the front of your thighs loading as you come down
bad: Don't let your lower back round off the pad at the bottom, stop before that happens

exercises.name: Dumbbell Split Squat
exercises.note: This one is new and it tests your balance as much as your legs. The set is over when your front knee starts drifting inwards or you need to grab something, even if that's at rep 6. Log the honest number. A fingertip on the rack for balance is fine for the first few sessions.

good: Drop straight down so the back knee hovers just off the floor, then drive through the front heel
The front leg's glute and thigh should be doing almost all of it
bad: Don't let the front knee cave inward as you stand up, that's the set finished

good: Heels on the ball, hips up, then pull the ball in toward your bum
Hamstrings and glutes hold the hips high the whole set
bad: Don't let your hips drop as the ball comes in

good: Chest stays glued to the pad, row the dumbbells to your hips
Pull your shoulder blades together at the top
bad: Don't lift your chest off the pad to move more weight

good: Push your knees out against the pads and pause before you let them back in
You should feel this on the outside of your hips, not your lower back
bad: Don't rock your body to swing the pads open

exercises.name: Assault Bike
exercises.note: Same easy effort as your treadmill walk, just a different machine so your legs get a break from the hill. If there's no assault bike free, any bike or the treadmill at the same effort is fine.

good: Steady pace you can hold the whole 20 minutes, arms working as well as legs
Legs and lungs ticking over, never gasping
bad: Don't start fast and fade, this is one steady effort

cards.title: You Earned This One
cards.body:
Back in April your form said sleep 4 out of 10 and stress 9 out of 10. That's why Cycle 1 was kept easy. Pushing hard on top of that would have cost you more than it gave you.

Now look at your last five sessions. Sleep 4 out of 5, stress 4 out of 5, every single time. Your habit tracker says 7 and a half hours most nights. That turned around, and you're the one who turned it.

That's the reason this cycle is heavier. Your body can take it now.

cards.title: What Changed And Why
cards.body:
Every lift in Cycle 1 said RPE 6. That's four reps left in the tank. You hit it honestly for three months, which is exactly what I asked for. The problem is nothing ever told you to go up, so from June the weight just sat there. That's my fault, not yours.

Now every lift says RPE 8. Two reps left instead of four. Same kind of reps, a lot more work.

Don't jump straight into it. Take the first two weeks to find your weights and sit closer to a 7 while you do. On the Romanian deadlift, the split squat and the leg press, stay at that easier end until week three. Those are the three where guessing wrong costs you the most.

cards.title: How To Move The Weight
cards.body:
The app never hands you a weight. You pick it and the effort target tells you if you got it right. Here's the whole system.

  • New movement? Start lighter than you think. Do the first set. Felt like a 6, go up. Felt like a 9, come down.
  • Same lift next time? Got all your reps at the target effort or easier, put a bit more on. Were at your limit or missed reps, stay on that weight and do it again.
  • Rough day? Take weight off. That isn't failing, that's you reading your own body, and it's the skill I actually want you to build.

Small jumps are enough. The smallest plate in the gym will do. This is the exact bit that got stuck last cycle, so this is the bit that matters most.

cards.title: Your Left Arm
cards.body:
You've told me about your left arm four times now. On the chest press your sets went 14, 14, 9 and then 9, 9, 5, and you wrote that your right arm was fine and could have kept going. I heard you, and this cycle is the answer.

The machine was half the problem. One stack for both arms, so the strong side carries the weak one until the weak one quits and the set is over. You're on dumbbells now. Each arm holds its own weight.

Two rules. On the incline press, pick the weight your left arm can finish every rep with and let the right work at that. On the single arm row, always start with the left. Whatever it does, the right one matches and doesn't go higher.

cards.title: Day 1 Will Bite
cards.body:
Day 1 has the hip thrust, the Romanian deadlift and the leg curl, all with a slow lower. The first couple of times you do it the back of your legs is going to be properly sore for three or four days. That's normal and it's not a reason to skip Day 3.

Two things would not be normal. If your pee goes dark, or if the soreness hasn't started easing off by day four, stop and message me before your next session.

cards.title: When You're Not Feeling It
cards.body:
Some days you'll walk in flat. Don't cancel the session, just shrink it.

  • Low readiness? Drop the effort target by one on the lifting. Leave the cardio as it is or just do less of it.
  • Short on time or energy? Do the first two lifts of that day and go home. That's the part that counts.
  • Order? Move the days around your week if you need to. Just leave a full rest day between any two sessions, and keep Day 1 and Day 3 at least two days apart. They're both leg days.
  • If the only way you can train is back to back days, put Day 2 in the middle.

cards.title: The Walk Is Yours
cards.body:
You've been adding 30 minutes on the treadmill after your sessions on your own, incline 4 at 5.5. Good idea, so I've written it in. It's the finisher on Day 2 now, and Day 3 ends on the bike instead so your legs get a break from the hill.

Here's how the walk grows. Count walks, not weeks.

  • Walks 1 to 6: 30 minutes, incline 4
  • Walks 7 to 12: 30 minutes, incline 6
  • Walk 13 onwards: 40 minutes, incline 6

Pace stays at 5.5 the whole way and only one thing changes at a time. Chase the incline number, not the feeling. It's supposed to get harder as it climbs. And don't hang off the handrails, that takes the work straight back out of it.

One honest thing. The walk is brilliant for your heart and your head, and it helps you recover between sessions. But it isn't what changes your body composition. That comes from what you eat. The walking supports it, it doesn't do it on its own.

cards.title: The Part The Gym Can't Do
cards.body:
You're training a lot harder this block, so protein matters more than it did. At your weight that's somewhere around 115 to 145 grams a day. Your tracker asks for 3 protein meals and you're logging 1 or 2. One proper protein source at every meal gets you most of the way there. Eggs, yoghurt, chicken, fish, beans, cottage cheese.

Water is your easiest win in the whole app. Target is 8 glasses and you're logging 2 to 4 most days. That one is just a habit, it isn't hard.

And about the no sugar habit you added yourself. You wrote that since you added it your intake went up twenty times, which genuinely made me laugh, but it's also telling you something. Don't ban it, halve it. Banned things always come back.
